title: The data lifecycle: generation, ingestion, storage, transformation and delivery

videos.script: A ride ends at Rua XV at eight in the morning, and the app charges for it and moves on. {{ride}} By the next morning that ride is a number in Marta's report, and this lesson follows it there. {{follow}} On the way it passes through five stages. It is born in a system that was built for something else. {{generation}} It is copied out without changing a thing. {{ingestion}} The copy is kept, and nobody ever edits it. {{storage}} Then it is cleaned, joined to its station's name, and counted. {{transformation}} And at the end, somebody reads it. {{delivery}} You build all five on your own machine, as four short programs writing into three directories. {{programs}} Then you run the copy twice, the way a retry would, and the report doubles without a word of complaint. {{twice}} You fix it, so that running it twice gives the same answer as running it once. {{fix}} Last, you take one number from the report and walk it back, row by row, to the app that made it. {{lineage}} A number you cannot walk back is a number you cannot defend. {{end}}
